title: skin-test parameters
description: Every tunable number in the rig. STRICT-COMPLETE: every property is required and additionalProperties is false everywhere, so a missing knob and a misspelt one both fail at the load seam rather than silently taking a default. Per-field validity (types, ranges, required, no strays) is enforced here; the cross-field residue a schema cannot express — non-degenerate seeds, a lapping skin having a direction to lap in, names matching the rule table — lives in Python (skinning/skin/parameters.py and skinning/rules.py).

classify.description: substrate.classify's two thresholds — WALL or ROOF from geometry alone.

margin.description: A horizontality within this of the halfway mark raises AmbiguousPart. Must stay below 0.5, or every part is ambiguous.

aspect.description: The two smallest oriented-bounding-box extents within this ratio means block-like — no clear thin direction — and raises AmbiguousPart. Strictly below 1: classify raises when extents[0] > aspect * extents[1] and extents is sorted ascending, so aspect = 1 makes that test unreachable and switches the block-like guard off entirely — a 1x1x1 cube then classifies as a wall.

fall.description: A wall's vertical face is exterior or interior when its normal's dot with the wall's own uphill direction exceeds this, and an end otherwise. A direction cosine, so within (0, 1); 0.707 is 45 deg.

reveal.description: The second allowance, metres. Where a cladding skin dies against a cornice it does not cover, or lines the cheeks of an opening cut through a wall, it stands this far off that surface instead of its own distance. One number shared by every skin that clads a facade, because it is a property of how a cladding system meets a substrate feature rather than of any one system. Strictly positive — see build.reveal_faces for which faces take it and build.skin_offsets for how it is applied.

skins.description: One entry per skin, in build order. Each `rules` must match a rule set in skinning/rules.py's RULES exactly — no defaults, either way. An entry with `select: "*"` is one skin per value of that rule set's key the substrate carries, so the number of skins built can exceed the number of entries.

name.description: Names the emitted OBJ and its manifest entry. A fanned-out skin (select: "*") names one per value found, as <name>-<value>.

rules.description: The rule set in skinning/rules.py RULES these numbers are built with. Several skins may name one rule set — two masonries at two allowances, a membrane per roof — which is why this is a field of its own and no longer the name.

select.description: Which instance of that rule set this skin is: the value of the metadata key the rule set declares (a roof zone, a cladding material), "*" for one skin per value the substrate carries, or null for a rule set that takes no selector. Checked against RULES in skinning/rules.check_skins, both ways round.

distance.description: Planar offset outward from the substrate, metres. Strictly positive — a zero-offset skin is coincident with the substrate.

drop.description: How far a lap hangs below the arris it springs from, metres, measured on the substrate. Zero switches that direction off.

out.description: How far a lap rises or runs sideways, metres, measured from the skin edge. Zero switches that direction off; build.py raises if both drop and out are zero on a skin whose rule set laps at all.

base.description: Height, metres, at which the finished skin is cut, keeping what is above — for a skin that stops at a datum (cladding at ground level) rather than on the miter it would take against an unskinned neighbour. null means no trim, and is NOT the same as 0.0: zero is a real height to trim at, whereas a zero drop or out is the feature switched off. Not a seed — a datum in the model, not a distance between surfaces — so check_seeds ignores it.

close.description: Widest tear, metres, that skin/clean.py will close with a gusset — a face that is not the offset of anything, bridging where the substrate had no thickness and the offset surfaces parted. Zero switches it off. A bound on a cleanup rather than a distance a surface is built to, so check_seeds ignores it; authored rather than derived, because the tear it exists for is 2 x distance across in plan but wider along its own sloped plane.
